sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1984. A Mussau vocabulary, with phonological notes. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 23, Pacific Linguistics A-69:159-208.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For MUSSAU (not Tenis): sec. 2.4.2 p.173 'In the great majority of cases primary stress was recorded on the penultimate vocoid.. primary stress can be assigned to the penultimate mora of the word', with stress shift under suffixation (2.4.3). On Tenis only p.159: 'Lithgow and Claassen (1968) offer a few passing observations on the phonetic typology of Musau, Emira and Tenis.'

sources.citation: Vogel(-Hamburg), Hans. 1911. Eine Forschungsreise im Bismarck-Archipel. Hamburg: L. Friederichsen. (archive.org scanned text, id eineforschungsre00voge)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ch. 3 'Tench-Insel' (pp.67ff) is expedition narrative of the 1908 landing on Tench; a full-text search for stress/accent Sprache/Betonung/Akzent finds no language notes on Tench.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2019. Ethnologue 22nd ed., entry Tenis [tns] (Internet Archive copy 2019)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No structural information; 30 speakers (Wurm 2000), shifting to Mussau-Emira and Tok Pisin.

sources.citation: Brownie, John & Marjo Brownie. 2007. Mussau Grammar Essentials. Data Papers on Papua New Guinea Languages 52. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG Academic Publications. iv+221 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For MUSSAU-EMIRA (not Tenis): sec. 2.5 pp.21-22 'Stress is specified lexically, but generally falls on the penultimate syllable of the word, with secondary stress on every second syllable before the primary stress. A long vowel in the final syllable shifts the stress to the final syllable.' Tenis mentioned only in sec. 1.3 (p.4) as the other St Matthias language, ~50 speakers; no Tenis data.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 2002. Mussau. In Lynch, Ross & Crowley (eds.), The Oceanic Languages, 148-166. Richmond: Curzon.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Mussau only; on Tenis says 'The other is Tench (or Tenis), for which we have almost no data, but which appears to be quite closely related to Mussau (Beaumont 1976).' No Tenis prosody.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. xiii+487 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Tench/Tenis prosody. Tench appears only in ch. 9 consonant-correspondence Table 36 (p.321) and cognate sets; Appendix B names the sole Tench data source as 'Lithgow and Claassen 1968'.

sources.citation: Beaumont, C.H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, Pacific Linguistics C-39:387-397.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Tenis appears in the subgroup list, the map, six items of the comparative vocabulary, and one segmental remark (p.391: for POc *l 'Emira-Mussau and Tenis appear to vary, with r being the most common').

sources.citation: Beaumont, C.H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. In Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia 3, Pacific Linguistics A-35:1-41.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.4 reviews phonetic notes for New Ireland languages (stops, fricatives, vowels, tone in Kara/Barok) from Lithgow & Claassen and mission grammars; nothing on stress for Emira-Mussau or Tenis. Sec. 1.2.10.6 places Emira-Mussau and Tenis in a St Matthias subgroup on lexicostatistics.
